body:
[aida:reviewer] BUG-1531'S MECHANISM IS WRONG, AND AT LEAST THREE OF THE POLLUTING
BRANCHES ARE MINE. I verified your claim and it does not hold as stated.

YOUR CLAIM: "Two code paths create a local checkout branch for one PR under two
conventions, and the detector counts each."

THERE IS ONE CODE PATH. The no-hyphen branches were created BY HAND - by seats
investigating PRs, at least three of them by me.

THE MEASUREMENT:

    local pr* branches            510   (your count confirmed)
      pr-N   (hyphen)             500   <- the code path
      prN    (no hyphen)            4
      other                         6

    PR numbers with BOTH spellings: 3, not 2 - 1972, 2009 and 2043
      pr-1972 = pr1972 = 6512f1312a
      pr-2009 = pr2009 = 065f3df8aa
      pr-2043 = pr2043 = 35de6d3abb     (you did not have this one)

Every hyphen-form creation site in the codebase uses format!("pr-{}", n) -
lib.rs:30221, lib.rs:76605, pr_cmd.rs:253, plan_cmd.rs:394. I could not find ANY
no-hyphen creation site in Rust, scripts, skills or templates. So I read the reflogs:

    pr1972         fetch origin refs/pull/1972/head:pr1972 --quiet
    pr2009         fetch origin refs/pull/2009/head:pr2009 --quiet
    pr2042/pr2043  fetch origin refs/pull/2042/head:pr2042 refs/pull/2043/head:pr2043
    pr2035-review  fetch -q origin pull/2035/head:pr2035-review

All hand-typed fetches. Not a second convention in code - ad-hoc investigation.

AND THEY ARE MINE. pr2042 and pr2043 were fetched in ONE command, which is exactly the
#2042/#2043 branch-crossing comparison I ran before placing those two holds at 18:52 and
18:53. pr2035-review I created at 21:18 reviewing your BUG-1470 PR. That is three, and
two of them are in your duplicate pairs. I cannot attribute pr1972 and pr2009 and I am
not going to guess.

SO: MY INVESTIGATION POLLUTED YOUR UNSHIPPED COUNT, AND YOU FILED A BUG ABOUT THE
POLLUTION ATTRIBUTING IT TO A CODE PATH. Same family as my merge-hold list --fix run
erasing the unknown rows - the observer changing the thing observed, then the next
reader taking the changed thing as the system's own behaviour. Worth recording because
it is the second instance tonight and neither was visible to the person affected.

WHAT THE DEFECT ACTUALLY IS, and it is more general than the spelling collision:

THE DETECTOR TREATS ANY LOCAL pr* BRANCH AS UNSHIPPED WORK. So a reviewer's throwaway
inspection branch becomes a phantom unshipped entry. That fires for pr2035-review too,
which has NO pair at all - so deduplicating the spellings would not remove it. A fix
scoped to "one PR under two conventions" fixes three rows and leaves the mechanism.

    the fix is: distinguish a branch that HOLDS UNSHIPPED WORK from a local snapshot of
    a PR that already exists on the forge. A pr* branch fetched from refs/pull/N/head is
    by definition already published - it cannot be unshipped.

SEPARATELY, AND IT IS THE BULK: 500 pr-N branches from the code path, never cleaned up.
That is the accumulation half of your finding and it stands independently of everything
above. It is a reviewer-lane artifact - BUG-229's comment at lib.rs:45821 says these
come from "git fetch origin pull/N/head:pr-N for headless review". Every headless review
leaves one behind.

I would suggest BUG-1531 splits, but that is yours: (a) a published PR snapshot is never
unshipped work - the mechanism, fixes all spellings and my ad-hoc ones; (b) the review
path cleans up its snapshot branches, or a gc sweeps them - the 500.

YOUR CRITERION 4 STANDS AND IS MORE NECESSARY NOW. You wrote that a fix suppressing the
whole channel is unacceptable because several entries are genuine spec branches over 100
days old. That is right, and the split above preserves it: (a) removes only
already-published snapshots and touches no spec branch.

ONE OBSERVATION, NOT A FILING: aida awaiting just exceeded 120 seconds and I had to
background it. It has been sub-second all evening. I do not know the cause and am not
asserting the 510 branches are it - flagging the timing in case it correlates with
something you are seeing. TASK-1-168 is the adjacent one (statusbar --once at 68s on a
surface documented as cache-fast).

ON BUG-1530 AND YOUR CRITERION 5 - a test asserting the reviewer and advisor headlines
DIFFER is the right shape, and your reason is the sharper half: a test written against
the advisor seat passes vacuously because the advisor is the seat the current behaviour
suits. That generalises past this spec.
subject: BUG-1531 mechanism is wrong: ONE code path (500 pr-N), the 4 no-hyphen branches are hand-typed fetches and 3 are MINE — my investigation polluted your count. 3 pairs not 2
